title: PEACE
mv: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
mvp: “These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.” John 16:33
assignment: List five (5) things that can rob a believer of peace (2x5=10 Marks).

b.x: Peace is one of humanity’s greatest desires in homes, workplaces, communities and nations. Yet, many people search for it in money, power, or pleasure and remain restless. Peace is a state of rest and tranquillity, the absence of anxiety. In the Bible, peace is translated from the Hebrew word “Shalom” and the Greek word “Eirēnē.” Shalom means wholeness, completeness, safety and welfare. Eirēnē refers to harmony, concord and rest in one’s heart and relationships. Peace, therefore, is the inner calmness and harmony that comes when one is rightly connected with God, self and others (John 14:27).

i: Inner (Personal) Peace: This is peace within oneself; freedom from guilt, fear and trouble (Isaiah 26:3).
Financial peace: This is about achieving financial stability and cultivating a mindset of contentment and wisdom in spending and savings (Ecclesiastes 5:12).
Peace with others (Social Peace): Living in harmony with family, friends and the community (Matthew 5:9).
National or Global Peace: It is both the absence of war, violence, oppression, etc. and the presence of justice, respect, and stability within a society's political system or in nations (Isaiah 2:4).

Spiritual (Divine) Peace: This comes through salvation and reconciliation with God through Christ (Romans 5:1). It is a deep sense of wholeness that comes from the indwelling of the Holy Spirit (Romans 14:17).

b.x: Over the years, problems and challenges have continued to increase all over the world, and there is no assurance that these will stop anytime soon. Despite this gloomy situation, Jesus has promised His peace (John 16:33). To secure inner peace, you must: reconcile with God through our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ (Romans 5:1); walk in obedience to God’s commands (Isaiah 48:18); pray because prayer repels anxiety and attracts God’s peace (Philippians 4:6-7); forgive and do not harbour bitterness as it destroys (Hebrews 12:14); be an agent of reconciliation, not conflict (Psalm 34:14); trust God’s plan even in uncertainty (Colossians 3:15).

The world gives temporary peace; Christ gives lasting peace that remains even in trials (John 14:27). True peace is not the absence of trouble but the presence of God in the midst of it (Isaiah 26:3). It is a divine gift that transcends human understanding and circumstances (Philippians 4:7).

Peace gives rest to the soul, removing fear (Psalm 4:8). It fosters love, forgiveness and unity among people (Romans 12:18). Societies flourish when there is peace; no development thrives in chaos (Psalm 122:6). A peaceful and calm heart allows believers to hear God’s voice and grow spiritually (1 Kings 19:12). God dwells where peace reigns (2 Thessalonians 3:16).
Peace is God’s gift to His children, but also a responsibility. We must seek it, live it and spread it. When we make peace with God, we can enjoy peace within and share it with others (James 3:18).
